metadata.title: Key Terms: Visualization Under Validation
metadata.lecture_opening_description: 32 terms for honest charts and misleading ones.

idea.text:
A chart is
a clear view of the data.
idea.triggerWords: a clear view of the data

numbers worked out on screen from stated inputs
a made-up run with a fixed seed, the same every time
numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured

defs_parts: Five labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a made-up run with a fixed seed, so it comes out the same every time.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A dashboard's layout argues before anyone takes in a number.
State the question first, then pick position or length for quantity.
Aleatoric is chance in the data, epistemic is doubt about the data.
Label every error bar, and draw uncertainty at equal visual weight.
Truncated, inverted and inconsistent axes change the story, not the data.
An evidence-grade chart shows what could prove the claim wrong.
bookends.command: Quiz me on chart terms. Give me one short case at a time, a chart described in two sentences. I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold the answer until I reply. Draw on aleatoric uncertainty, epistemic uncertainty, truncated axes, axis inversion, inconsistent axes, cherry-picked window, missing baseline, selective uncertainty, and false precision.
checks: Check: each case fit one term, and you named it before the answer came.
Check: Claude said why the look-alike term did not fit the case.
